related_questions.question: How common is myocarditis in children?

text_blocks.snippet: Myocarditis in children is rare. While it can occur at any age, it's slightly more common in older children and adults, though it can be more severe in newborns and young infants. The incidence rate in children is estimated to be around 1 to 2 cases per 100,000 children per year, with some studies reporting a rising trend.
snippet_highlighted_words: 1 to 2 cases per 100,000 children per year

list.title: Rarity:
list.snippet: Myocarditis is not a common diagnosis in children.

list.title: Age Distribution:
list.snippet: While it can affect all ages, there's a bimodal distribution with peaks in infancy and mid-teenage years.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: Myocarditis can range from mild to severe, with some cases requiring hospitalization.

list.title: Causes:
list.snippet: Most cases are caused by viral infections, but other factors can also trigger inflammation.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms can mimic a viral infection initially, but may also include chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue.

list.title: Underlying Conditions:
list.snippet: In rare instances, conditions like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis can be associated with myocarditis.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: The SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes COVID-19, can also lead to myocarditis, but this is still being studied.

list.title: Sudden Cardiac Death:
list.snippet: Myocarditis is a recognized cause of sudden cardiac death in children and young adults, particularly athletes.
